atoms.text: The Giant’s Causeway is located in Northern Ireland and is made out of more than 40,000 hexagonal shaped columns of rock. These rock formations can be found in not only Northern Ireland but also on the Isle of Staffa, located in Scotland.

atoms.text: There are both old myths and scientific theories that attempt to explain how and why the landscape on both islands looks the way it does. In the following text, you will read about the myth of the Giant Finn McCool and his role in the creation of the Giant’s Causeway.

atoms.text: As the myth goes, a giant living in Northern Ireland, Finn McCool, built the Giant’s Causeway — a feat which, to this day, has made him one of the most famous mythological characters of the island.

Across the water, in Scotland, lived another giant, Benandonner. According to the myth, the two giants were rivals and often shouted insults at each other across the sea. One day, Finn McCool, fed up with Benandonner, started to throw rocks into the sea. He noticed the rocks formed a sort of bridge, or causeway, that would enable him to walk over the sea to Scotland where he could finally confront his nemesis.
atoms.sound: Across the water, in Scotland, lived another giant, Benandonner. According to the myth, the two giants were rivals and often shouted insults at each other across the sea. One day, Finn McCool, fed up with Benandonner, started to throw rocks into the sea. He noticed the rocks formed a sort of bridge, or causeway, that would enable him to walk over the sea to Scotland where he could finally confront his nemesis.

atoms.text: Finn McCool was ready to challenge his rival to a proper fight but realised that he had underestimated his opponent. Benandonner was a massive giant, far taller than Finn himself, and it became evident quickly that Finn could not win.

Luckily, Finn McCool’s wife Oonagh was a very clever woman. Quick as you like, she had a plan to trick Benandonner into returning to Scotland without fighting her husband. She dressed her husband Finn McCool as a giant baby and put him in a crib.
atoms.sound: Luckily, Finn McCool’s wife Oonagh was a very clever woman. Quick as you like, she had a plan to trick Benandonner into returning to Scotland without fighting her husband. She dressed her husband Finn McCool as a giant baby and put him in a crib.

atoms.text: Benandonner crossed the causeway and arrived at the McCool’s house in Ireland. He saw Oonagh and her giant baby and was horrified. If the baby was already so big, what would the dad be like? Surely Finn McCool must be even taller than himself!

Benandonner turned tail and ran back to Scotland. In fear of the massive Finn McCool, he destroyed the causeway and severed the only connection between Scotland and Ireland. In his rush, he lost one of his boots. This boot and the other rocks along the coastline reaching into the water are the last witnesses to the giants’ legendary rivalry.
